correctness.rationale: The direct ordered-difference count gives the Shrikhande (16,6,2,2) parameters. For independent C of size t, the sums of a_x and a_x(a_x-1)/2 prove t<=4, and t=4 forces every outside a_x=2, excluding any PCF four-coloring. Two independently written certificate programs verify a proper PCF five-coloring of S. A row/column missing-color multiplicity obstruction excludes PCF five-colorings of R; two independent checks verify the explicit proper PCF six-coloring. The two lower-bound arguments cover every smaller palette, not merely tested colorings.

value.rationale: The Shrikhande and rook graphs are the distinguished nonisomorphic strongly regular pair with identical order, degree and common-neighbor parameters (16,6,2,2). Determining a sharp and previously unlocated PCF value for Shrikhande creates a motivated exact invariant separating these graphs, while the rook equality is known and credited. The proof identifies why identical two-common-neighbor data forces a shared 4-color obstruction but permits different optimal upper constructions; the fact is a natural complete finite classification rather than an arbitrary slice.
